# gitmoap_repository_pipeline_files (Data Source)

List the pipelines declared at a ref. Every pipeline the `.gitmoap/pipelines/` files declare at a branch, a tag or a full ref — the default branch when none is named — with the directory and the file that declare it, whether it validates, whether the default branch registers it, and whether its directory's files differ from the default branch's. Anyone who can read the repository's pipelines may list them, without signing in on a public repository.

The token needs `pipeline:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_pipeline_files" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository id

### Optional

- `ref` (String) A branch, a tag or a full ref; the default branch when absent

### Read-Only

- `commit_sha` (String) The commit the ref pointed at; every pipeline in the listing was read there.
- `items` (Attributes List) One page of the pipelines, in name order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `blob_sha` (String) That file's git object id at this ref — what a commit that edits it names as
`expected_blob_sha`.
- `changed_from_default` (Boolean) Whether any file of its namespace differs from the default branch's — always `false` on the
default branch itself.
- `directory` (String) The directory its namespace is — every `.hcl` file in it reads as one.
- `error_count` (Number) How many errors it has.
- `name` (String)
- `path` (String) The file its `pipeline` block is in, from the repository's root.
- `pipeline_id` (String)
- `registration` (String) Whether a pipeline declared at a ref is one of the pipelines the repository's default branch
registers.
- `valid` (Boolean) Whether the pipeline reads, binds and validates with no error.
- `warning_count` (Number) How many warnings it has. A warning never stops a pipeline from running.
